He had the eye / that finds the fish where sky and water meet; / he met the tide each day; he did defy / the wave that hit the ship, the dark, the sleet. // He is at sea this dusk. I keep awake; / I keep the tea but wait, the tide my guide, / then if my faith might fetch him back, I make / the teacup hiss, the chair set by my side. // The dark is thick. The teacup keeps the hiss. / I hear the deck; I hear the pier; I wait. / The dead ask this: that we recite the kiss, / the arm that fed me, then the arm that ate. // My father kept the deep. The deep kept him. / I keep the tea.
